In this video, I teach you The Confusion Compass Method, a simple technique for turning confusion into targeted questions that helps you learn faster.

my mother taught me this at age 6. she wouldn't help me with my homework unless i had a specific question to ask about what i didn't understand. by figuring out the question i wanted to ask her i figured out the answer on my own
The problem is that 99% of the time I have to learn things that I don't care about. Like, at all.
This makes me realize the best teachers I had in high school were those that triggered our minds by asking questions not just reading us by power point.
If normal daily responsibilities sometimes feel unbelievably overwhelming, Anwen Reid’s anxiety quiz may help you understand why. It’s quick, free and surprisingly detailed.

While studying about  psychology and how our brain is designed to learn. 

The frustration and agitation you feel while learning anything new is how our brain is originally designed to learn. 

And we go through 4 cycles to learn and master any thing (skill). e.g: driving a car.

1) Unconscious Incompetent: you don't know, what you don't know. (Stage of Ignorance) 
> [Not knowing how to Drive]

2)
Naturally confused ❎ Naturally Curious ✅
I felt this one. Success is simple you either outwork your excuses or you lose. The Other Side of Order by Steven Humsfeld pushed me to show up even on the days where motivation is zero

To summarise this:
CURIOSITY is an element when added to anything can enhance it's flavor giving a better understanding of the topic and maybe make the process enjoyable.

Reframing confusion as just a stack of unorganized data is genius. Most of us hit a wall, feel overwhelmed, and think the solution is to read more chapters, basically dumping an entire extra mountain of disconnected data onto the pile. No wonder we stay generally confused for months.

Guys, every success takes time.

 The moment you start looking for short cut, that's when your progress starts to decline.

Only CONSISTENCY can get you to your goal. 

Cheers guys
So basically, if I feel confused I should actually write out a question asking what makes me confused and think about how to answer it?
